To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DNNs can learn class-wise predictive patterns, which can be visualized in the input space, and the learned patterns are different under different training conditions.

(i) DNNs trained in the natural, adversarial and backdoor settings learn distinct patterns in the input pixel space; (ii) adversarial training simplifies the learned patterns in the input; and (iii) backdoored models can be attacked by exploiting the learned patterns in our method.

DNNs: (1) trained on natural (i.e. non-backdoored, non-adversarial) data learn abstract shape patterns along with some texture; (2) trained on backdoored data learn a small but predictive pattern for the target backdoor class; and (3) adversarially trained learn more simplified shape-based patterns.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the class-wise patterns in the input (pixel) space learned by DNN models.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DNNs learn a combination of shapes and textures, and adversarially trained DNNs tend to learn more shapes.
DNNs are able to learn class-wise patterns in the pixel space, which is the most intuitive level for human understanding.
DNNs learn class-wise predictive patterns, which can be exploited to attack the models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a method to reveal the class-wise patterns in the input (pixel) space, which can help us understand what a DNN has learned from the training data and how it makes decisions.
DNNs learn class-wise predictive patterns that are highly interpretable in the input space, regardless of whether the model is trained on natural data, backdoored or adversarially.
we show that DNs learn predictive patterns in the image space, and these patterns can be readily used to “backdoor attack” the model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNNs learn class-wise predictive patterns, and these patterns can be readily exploited by backdoor attacks.
class-wise patterns in the input (pixel) space can be a powerful tool for understanding and attacking DNNs.
DNNs learn class-wise predictive patterns that are not obvious to humans, and such patterns are not only useful for understanding DNNs but also can be exploited by adversaries.
